top_comments.author: @brannonboren323
top_comments.text:
I co-authored the first story bible for Halo and was a writer on Halo: Combat Evolved. I specifically wrote the bible's specs for the Halo ring, so I can tell you the bible indicated the ring spins fast enough to provide almost Earth-normal gravity (approximately .93 that of Earth).

The caveat about ancient tech "gravity wells" in the ring was added to the write-up to cover any scientific discrepancies that might arise later, so we could say the "gravity tech" made up the difference. But the ring was intended to generate most of its gravity from spin.

This may have been contradicted later (I left the franchise in 2003), but I did think about it and write it down at the very start (before the game was even released).

Really enjoyed your walk through of the various incarnations of this concept!

top_comments.author: @mikip3242
top_comments.text:
Astrophysicist here. So actually there is a problem with all this: the expansion of the universe. Even if you travel close to the speed of light, there are regions that we currently know about that are beyond a causal cosmological horizon. For example, Galaxies beyond the Virgo cluster are unreachable even if you launched today at 99.9999999999% the speed of light.

Distances between distant galaxies scale more quickly than the time It takes you to reach them. So the expansion of the universe kills the dream.

Your calculations are nice until you go beyond Andromeda. Then things need significantly more time to be reached than what you expect by special relativity in a static universe alone, and things get worse after that, until you basically need infinite proper time to reach the stuff located just at this cosmological horizon.

In summary: We are caged because of the expansion of the universe.
